stem: A provider orders an aerobic culture from an open draining wound. Which specimen-collection approach is most appropriate?

options.A: Scrape dried drainage from intact skin beside the wound and submit it in a dry container because surface material is the preferred culture source.
options.B: Swab the removed dressing because organisms on an old dressing represent the wound more accurately than material collected from the wound itself.
options.C: Swab intact periwound skin because normal skin flora identify the organism responsible for infection within the draining wound.
options.D: Collect purulent material or a specimen directly from the wound with the laboratory-approved sterile system and place it in the designated transport medium.

rationale: ARUP Test 0060132 accepts aspirate, purulent material, or a swab specimen for wound culture. Purulent material is transferred to an appropriate sterile/transport container, and swabs are placed in ESwab transport medium; dry swabs are unacceptable. Therefore D is correct because it samples the wound itself and uses the laboratory-designated transport system. A, B and C preferentially sample dried surface material, an old dressing, or intact surrounding skin rather than the ordered wound specimen.
educational_objective: Collect an appropriate wound-culture specimen directly from the wound using the laboratory-designated sterile transport system.

source_original.stem: A provider orders an aerobic culture from an open draining wound. Which specimen-collection approach is most appropriate?

options.A: Scrape dried drainage from intact skin beside the wound and submit it in a dry container because surface material is the preferred culture source.
options.B: Swab the removed dressing because organisms on an old dressing represent the wound more accurately than material collected from the wound itself.
options.C: Swab intact periwound skin because normal skin flora identify the organism responsible for infection within the draining wound.
options.D: Collect purulent material or a specimen directly from the wound with the laboratory-approved sterile system and place it in the designated transport medium.

source_original.rationale: ARUP's wound-culture collection instructions call for purulent material/aspirate or a swab specimen collected from the wound and placed in the designated transport system. Option D samples the actual wound rather than old dressing material or intact surrounding skin. Options A, B, and C preferentially sample surface contamination or normal flora and do not follow the laboratory collection method. NCSBN places obtaining nonblood specimens for diagnostic testing under Reduction of Risk Potential.
source_original.source_detail: ARUP Test 0060132, Wound Culture and Gram Stain — Specimen Required: collect aspirate/purulent material or a swab specimen from the wound; swab specimens are placed in the laboratory-designated ESwab transport medium. Anaerobic culture requires appropriate deeper specimen/transport when indicated. Current ARUP Laboratories test directory entry 0060132; collection requirements live-rechecked 2026-08-15. Blueprint corrected to Reduction of Risk Potential because the item tests collection of a nonblood diagnostic specimen, an explicit 2026 NCSBN laboratory-values activity. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Reduction of Risk Potential: diagnostic probability tools, laboratory/tumor-marker interpretation, ECG/lab monitoring and potential complications. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained construct/key; verified current ARUP specimen types/transport and removed any implication that surface material or old dressings are preferred specimens.
